AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 15, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685
DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32
OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  5:00 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8056-015-007 Negotiating parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Michael F G Trust; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Carina Montes
  Director of Human Resources

FLAG SALUTE
  Theresa Devoy
  City Clerk

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS – None.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Mayor’s Message to Class of 2021.

  3.  Little Free Libraries Ribbon Cutting.
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of May 25,
  2021 and June 1, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period May 2, 2021 – May 15,
  2021, in the total amount of $907,627.61. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period May
  27, through June 9, 2021, in the total amount of $1,349,470.74. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Victor Escobar.
  830-05

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 21-1726 – APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT – MERCY HOUSING PROJECT - Staff recommends City Council accept for second
  reading and adopt Ordinance No. 21-1726, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT WITH
  MERCY HOUSING CALIFORNIA RELATED TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE +/- 1.5 ACRE
  PROPERTY AT SAN ANTONIO DRIVE AND FOSTER ROAD; AND MAKING FINDINGS
  CONSISTENT WITH AND PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65867.5. 810-13/1405-
  01

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 6 - RESIDENTIAL USED MOTOR OIL COLLECTION PROGRAM -
  Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 6 with Waste Management Curbside, LLC for
  Used Oil Collection Program services, in an amount not to exceed $6,000 per year through June 30,
  2022; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 810-23/1065-04-01

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 6 – GRANT RESEARCH AND WRITING SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 6 with Blais and Associates, Inc., in an amount not
  to exceed $50,000 per Fiscal Year for grant research and writing services from July 1, 2021 through
  June 30, 2023; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a
  form approved by the City Attorney. 623/810-02

  Report

  9.  2021 APPLICATIONS FOR RETAIL FIREWORKS SALES PERMITS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the organizations eligible to obtain retail fireworks permits and authorize the issuance of
  permits. 612-08

  Report

  10. GRANT FOR EASEMENT AND CONVEYANCE OF SUPPORT INFRASTRUCTURE TO SOUTHERN
  CALIFORNIA EDISON TO SERVICE NEW ELECTRIC BUS CHARGING FACILITIES AT 12650
   IMPERIAL HIGHWAY – Staff recommends City Council approve granting an underground utility
  easement and the conveyance of the support structure for the existing Electrical Transformer at the
  Norwalk/ Santa Fe Springs Metrolink Station Parking lot at 12650 Imperial Highway, to Southern
  California Edison for service to the new electric bus charging stations and authorize the Mayor to sign
  documents as approved by the City Attorney. 905-06

  Report

11. RESOLUTION NO. 21-29 – STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY – Staff recommends City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 21-29, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  ADOPTING THE 2021/22 STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  TREASURER TO INVEST AND REINVEST IDLE MONIES OF THE CITY OF NORWALK IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE 2021/22 STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY. 624

  Report

12. RESOLUTION NO. 21-30 - ADOPTION OF ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2021/22 – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution 21-30, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22. 604

  Report

13. RESOLUTION NO. 21-31 – ADOPTING PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 – Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution 21-31, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING THE PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22. 634

  Report

  Report

14. RESOLUTION NO. 21-32 - ADVISORY BODY PROCEDURES UPDATE – ADDING FIVE POSITIONS
  TO THE PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-
  32, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-61, TO ADD FIVE ADDITIONAL MEMBERS TO THE PUBLIC SAFETY
  COMMISSION. 265

  Report

15. AGREEMENT - COST-SHARING AND REIMBURSEMENT - PUBLIC OUTREACH SERVICES FOR
  IMPROVEMENTS ON THE INTERSTATE-605 FREEWAY PROJECT - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the cost sharing and reimbursement agreement among the Cities of La Mirada, Santa Fe
  Springs, Downey, Norwalk, and Commerce to provide public outreach within the represented
  communities; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and any amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  1015-04

  Report

16. AWARD CONTRACT – CITYWIDE INSPECTION SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council award a
  contract to Onward Engineering in the amount of $163,800 for citywide inspection services; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the contract, and any amendments, provided there is funding in
  the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 310-02

  Report

17. RESOLUTION NO. 21-36 – CHILD CARE SERVICES CONTRACT EXTENSION – Staff recommends
  City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-36, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING CHILD CARE CONTRACT EXTENSION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF
  PUBLIC SOCIAL SERVICES FOR FUNDING OF THE CalWORKS STAGE 1 CHILD CARE
  DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/2022; and
   b.  authorize the City Manager to execute the contract extension and any other amendments,
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 425-01

  Report

  18. RESOLUTION NO. 21-37 - BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME
  HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PLANNING CONTRACT SERVICES – Staff recommends City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 21-37, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED BUDGET TO ADD
  LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PLANNING CONTRACT
  SERVICES, in the amount of $188,000. 320

  Report

  19. RESOLUTION NO. 21-39 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ALLOCATING FUNDING FOR PROJECT NO.
  7926 LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM PHASE 1 ZONE 32 - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 21-39, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED BUDGET
  TO APPROPRIATE TRANSPORTATION DEVELOPMENT ACT ARTICLE 3 FUNDS TO PROJECT NO.
  7926 PHASE 1, ZONE 32 - LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM, in the amount of
  $140,400. 610/1005-04-7926

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  20. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  21. RESOLUTION NO. 21-33 - SETTING SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 AND
  ORDERING THAT SUCH CHARGE BE COLLECTED ON THE TAX ROLL – Staff recommends City
  Council consider adopting Resolution No. 21-33, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE ANNUAL SEWER REPORT AND LEVYING AN ANNUAL
  SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 13.14 OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AND ORDERING THE ANNUAL SEWER SERVICE CHARGE TO BE
  COLLECTED ON THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TAX ROLL. 637

  Report

  22. RESOLUTION NO. 21-34 – ADOPTING AND SUBMITTING THE CITY’S 2020 URBAN WATER
  MANAGEMENT PLAN AND 2020 WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN TO THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-34, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK ADOPTING AND SUBMITTING THE CITY’S 2020 URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT
  PLAN AND 2020 WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN TO THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to submit the 2020 Urban Water Management Plan
  and Water Shortage Contingency Plan to the California Department of Water Resources. 1070-07

  Report

  23. RESOLUTION NO. 21-35 - ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE CITY’S ANNUAL BUDGET FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2021/22; AND RESOLUTION NO. 21-38 – ADOPTING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22
  SALARY SCHEDULE FOR GENERAL AND HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE
  MANAGEMENT AND MID-MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-35, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
   NORWALK ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2021/22; and

  b.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-38, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AMENDING AND ADOPTING FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 SALARY SCHEDULE FOR
  GENERAL AND HOURLY UNIT EMPLOYEES AND EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT AND MID-
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES. 610

  Report

REPORT

  24. SPECIAL DIRECTIVES OF DISTRICT ATTORNEY GASCON – Receive and file.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated June 10, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
